book.principiamagica.principia.name: Principia
book.principiamagica.principia.the_wet_c: The scribe calls them *me*. I call them axioms: laws that need no proof, only obedience. Carve the purpose while the clay is wet, with something of that purpose pressed in: grain for the harvest, a sapling for the felling. Then fire it. Wet clay can still be persuaded. Fired clay cannot.

*Enki kept the decrees in his house in Eridu: the decree of the plough, the decree of the axe, the decree of kingship, the decree of the destruction of cities. Each could be held in the hand. Each could be given away.*

Clay holds a law, but law alone does not move. The old makers mixed in flesh: a god's, if the tablet is to be believed. I have only what the dead leave behind. It will have to do. I would rather not think about what the clay remembers of it.

*They slew We-ila, the god who had reason. In his flesh and blood they mixed the clay. From his flesh came the ghost, and the ghost remembered. So man was made, to bear the basket in the gods' place.*
The clay by the river bears marks: wedges, rows of them, too regular to be chance. I have started copying them here. If they are words, someone meant them to last.
*In the beginning the gods laboured, and the labour was heavy. They dug the rivers. They bore the baskets. And they wept beneath the weight.*
Wood for the bones, quickened clay for the sinews. When I set it down it turned its head toward me. Nothing more. It does not know what it is for. It only knows that I am here.

Place the golem on a block face and it stands there for good. It never wanders off and it never fades.
\
\
Without an axiom it has no purpose. It stays where it is put, or follows you if you ask it to. It cannot work until it is given an axiom.
*Fourteen pieces of clay she pinched off. Seven on the right, seven on the left. Between them she set the brick.*
A cut reed would do, but copper holds its edge. With this I can carve the clay, and, if the tablets are right, command what the clay holds.
*The reed is cut, the clay is wet, the word goes in. What is pressed in the clay does not leave it.*

As a crafting tool, the stylus is never consumed: it returns to your grid after every recipe that uses it.
\
\
As a configuration tool, it selects a golem, carves its work boundaries and links its containers.
A blank tablet. The scribe treats wet clay as something that *listens*.
*Wet clay is open. It takes the word and the thumbprint and the fly that lands on it. Do not let it hear what you do not mean.*
